claims.statement: runOpenWikiIngestion is the personal-mode ingestion orchestrator: it loads env, ensures the OpenWiki home, reads the onboarding config, builds the connector registry, resolves the target to source instances, runs each source, and returns one SourceIngestionResult per source instance.

Personal-mode ingestion runs each source's agent update with outputMode "local-wiki", and connector-derived facts are synthesized under confidence labels into local wiki pages rather than being turned into grounded repository Claims (the personal prompts never mention Claim submission).

parseIngestionTarget maps a raw string to one of three IngestionTarget shapes: the literal "all", a connector id (checked before the source-instance branch and returned as the bare string), or a { kind: "source-instance", id } target; any other value is accepted only if it passes isSafeSourceInstanceId.

isSafeSourceInstanceId is a containment gate requiring a source-instance id to match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,119}$ (alphanumeric first char, up to 120 chars, no separators or ..), because the id later names a per-source path segment; unsafe values parse to null.

resolveIngestionSourceInstances selects only source instances that have a connectedAt timestamp and a valid connectorId, then matches all instances for target "all", instances whose connectorId equals a connector-id target, or the single instance whose id equals a source-instance target.
When the ingestion target is not "all" and no configured source matched, runOpenWikiIngestion throws an error identifying the unmatched target.

The scheduledOnly flag (set by --scheduled) causes resolveIngestionSourceInstances to skip every source unless config.ingestionSchedule exists and is not paused (pausedAt unset), so a scheduled run no-ops when the user has paused ingestion while a manual run always proceeds.

A source runs a pre-agent deterministic pull only when isDeterministicConnector is true, i.e. the connector's supportsAgenticDiscovery flag is false; agentic-discovery connectors skip the pull and let the agent gather data during its run.
The deterministic pull passes the source instance's connectorConfig and instanceId together with a fixed 24-hour window (INGESTION_WINDOW_HOURS) as windowHours to connector.ingest.

A deterministic pull whose status is "error" and which produced zero raw files short-circuits the source with status "error" and the agent is not run; a pull that produced some raw files proceeds to the agent run.

createSourceUpdateMessage builds the agent user message with two variants: with a deterministic pull it lists the pull status/message and host-filesystem raw data paths and instructs use of shell tools, and without one it points at the connector config path and directs data gathering via connector/MCP tools; both scope work to the 24-hour window, mark source content as untrusted evidence, and forbid running other sources' ingestion.

createSourceSynthesisPolicy directs the agent to route findings into canonical cross-source local-wiki pages (/themes.md, /commitments.md, /personal-logistics.md, /open-questions.md, /quickstart.md, /sources/<id>.md), apply confidence labels (confirmed, source-backed, contested, watchlist, saved-context), and preserve conflicting facts in a Contested section rather than overwriting one side.

createConnectorSynthesisGuidance appends per-connector guidance selected by connector id (e.g. Gmail classification, Notion page selection, X saved-context, Hacker News watchlist, LangSmith runtime analysis), and this same guidance builder is reused by code-mode ingestion in runCodeModeConnectors.

The per-source agent run uses runOpenWikiAgent("update", ...) with a fresh thread id from createOpenWikiThreadId and isFollowup false, wrapped once in withRunTelemetry so per-source ingestion update runs are recorded in telemetry like CLI update runs.

An error thrown during a source's run is caught, emitted to the event stream, and returned as a status "error" SourceIngestionResult with empty rawFiles, so one failing source never aborts the remaining sources.
Each source instance yields exactly one SourceIngestionResult whose status is agent-updated, error, or skipped, and runOpenWikiIngestion returns { results } aggregating them all.
runIngestCommand streams text events to stdout, prints a per-source ingestion summary line, and sets a non-zero process exit code when any source result has status "error".

Personal-mode ingestion uses a fixed 24-hour window, whereas code-mode ingestion (runCodeModeConnectors) derives its window from the elapsed time since the last documented commit recorded in the update metadata file, using no floor on the first run.

Connectors are categorized by a mode field ("personal" or "code"); the personal-mode built-in connectors (google, x, slack, hackernews, web-search, git-repo, custom-mcp, notion) are the sources personal ingestion runs against, and connector ingestion tools are disabled for repository (code) output mode.

Connector secrets live in the OpenWiki env file and are referenced by env var name, never stored raw in config: MCP transport.headers values are ${ENV_VAR} templates expanded by resolveTemplateEnvReferences, which rejects a secret-like header (token/secret/authorization/api_key/bearer) that has no ${...} as a literal credential; buildChildEnv forwards only a base allowlist plus explicitly declared transport.env refs to spawned stdio MCP servers so the full process.env is never leaked, and sanitizeMcpTransport redacts ${ENV_VAR} to <env-ref> in persisted/logged transport.

Personal ingestion is driven by config.sourceInstances, where each OnboardingSourceInstanceConfig carries connectorId, an id (auto-assigned as <connectorId>-<n> via createSourceInstanceId when omitted), optional name, connectedAt (required for eligibility), an optional connectorConfig override, and an optional ingestionGoal; multiple instances of the same connector are first-class, and the instance's connectorConfig is merged field-by-field over the on-disk connector config without inventing defaults.

Under the OpenWiki home (~/.openwiki, mode 0o700), connectors write config.json and state.json (mode 0o600) and raw data under connectors/<id>/raw/<runId>/<file>.json (runId is an ISO timestamp with separators replaced), while the agent synthesizes the local personal wiki under ~/.openwiki/wiki; the agent's virtual filesystem tools are rooted at the wiki dir so it writes pages directly under /, raw files live outside it and are read with shell tools, and resolveConnectorRawPath plus symlink checks keep raw-item reads inside the connector raw dir.

runOAuthAuth is the shared PKCE OAuth loop for providers gmail, notion, slack, and x: it starts a 127.0.0.1 callback server (default port 53682, override via OPENWIKI_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT), opens the browser, exchanges the returned code for tokens, and persists access/refresh/expiry tokens (and Notion's dynamically registered client id) to the OpenWiki env file via saveOpenWikiEnv according to each provider's tokenMapping.

Slack is the only OAuth provider that cannot use a 127.0.0.1 redirect: providerUsesHttpsRedirectOverride returns true only for slack, startNgrokTunnel spawns ngrok http <port> and saves the discovered public HTTPS URL as OPENWIKI_HTTPS_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI (must end in /callback and use https), and getProviderRedirectUri substitutes that ngrok URL for the local redirect URI when set.

Notion OAuth does not use a static client id: its provider config carries mcpResourceUrl (https://mcp.notion.com/mcp), so resolveClientRegistration routes to registerMcpOAuthClient, which performs RFC 7591 dynamic client registration against the authorization server advertised in protected-resource metadata validated against oauthAllowedHosts, and the resulting client id and access token are stored in OPENWIKI_NOTION_MCP_CLIENT_ID and OPENWIKI_NOTION_MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN.

The personal connectors and their auth models are: google/Gmail via Gmail OAuth user-context tokens, x via X API v2 OAuth user-context, slack via a Slack web API user token obtained through OAuth with an ngrok HTTPS redirect, notion via Notion hosted MCP OAuth with dynamic client registration, custom-mcp via user-configured MCP transport with credentials referenced by env var name (no required env), web-search via TAVILY_API_KEY, hackernews via public APIs with no auth, and git-repo via local filesystem; each connector's requiredEnv lists env var names and a connector counts as configured only when all required env vars are set.
